definitions.explanation: A {鍋|なべ} dish in which chicken and vegetables are simmered in water (no seasoning broth) and eaten with ponzu sauce. Particularly associated with Hakata (Fukuoka) and Kansai cuisine.

examples.japanese: {今夜|こんや}は{水炊|みずた}きにしよう。
{博多|はかた}の{水炊|みずた}きは{鶏|とり}の{旨味|うまみ}が{濃|こ}い。
examples.english: Hakata-style mizutaki has a rich chicken flavor.

examples.japanese: {水炊|みずた}きはポン{酢|ず}と{薬味|やくみ}でさっぱりと{食|た}べるのが{定番|ていばん}だ。
examples.english: It's standard to eat mizutaki refreshingly with ponzu and condiments.

notes:
Compound of {水|みず} (water) + {炊|た}く (to simmer/cook). The defining feature is that the broth starts as plain water — flavor comes from the chicken itself.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {博多|はかた}{水炊|みずた}き: Hakata-style mizutaki
- {鶏|とり}の{水炊|みずた}き: chicken mizutaki
- {水炊|みずた}きの{出汁|だし}: mizutaki broth
- ポン{酢|ず}で{食|た}べる: to eat with ponzu

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {寄|よ}せ{鍋|なべ}: mixed hot pot — uses a seasoned broth and many ingredients
- ちゃんこ{鍋|なべ}: chanko nabe — sumo-wrestler style hot pot
- しゃぶしゃぶ: shabu-shabu — thin meat dipped in hot broth
